datasets.label: Wallet app
datasets.tagline: Mobile wallet: sign up, top up, pay bills, buy e-load.

ui.about: This is a made-up (synthetic) sample that imitates a mobile wallet app: {users} users in {groups} groups register, log in, top up and buy {nprod} kinds of products ({products}) on the app and the web, from {start} to {end}. Problems were planted on purpose so Squint has something real to find: one-time codes that did not arrive for eight hours on Oct 9, individual traders abandoning Send money at checkout about half the time, fraudster accounts sharing devices, a payment tracker that went silent on one app version, lost rows on one day, an unmapped event property and a double-fired checkout event. Large business top-ups and e-load buying by store owners are also planted, as normal behavior that is not a problem. No real customer data is included.
ui.ask_placeholder: Ask about this dataset, for example: Why do sign-ups stall on Oct 9?
plain: Large business top up large amounts

how.examples: OTP code or Checkout and PIN

Stalled at the OTP code.who: People who asked for a one-time code more than once and still did not get through.
Stalled at the OTP code.todo: Check that codes arrive. These people are one step from signing up.
Stalled at the OTP code.biz: Every person stuck here is a sign-up lost before it starts.

High-value top-uppers.who: People who top up large amounts.
High-value top-uppers.todo: Keep their top-up path fast and reliable. A failure here costs the most.
High-value top-uppers.biz: Few people, but the largest top-ups, so one failure here costs more than anywhere else.

Load-first store owners.who: Store owners whose first purchase is phone load for their customers.
Load-first store owners.todo: Keep E-load one tap away. It is how they start.
Load-first store owners.biz: Phone load is how these stores start buying, so a broken load flow loses the store.

Straight-through completers.who: People who finish what they start without trouble.
Straight-through completers.todo: Nothing to fix. Use them as the benchmark for the other groups.
Straight-through completers.biz: The healthy core: they keep volume steady and set the benchmark.

Price-checkers, register later.who: People who look at prices before they sign up.
Price-checkers, register later.todo: Show prices early. They are deciding whether to join.
Price-checkers, register later.biz: Future sign-ups, not lost customers. Showing prices early helps them decide.

Other.who: People who do not fit a simple pattern.
Other.todo: No action. Look again if this group grows.
Other.biz: No business action needed unless this group grows.

datasets.label: Dining app
datasets.tagline: Food ordering and table booking: sign up, book a table, order dishes.

ui.about: This is a made-up (synthetic) sample that imitates a food ordering and table booking app: {users} users in {groups} groups sign up, book tables and order {nprod} kinds of dishes ({products}) on the app, from {start} to {end}. Everyone adds a payment method after signing up, when they book a table. Problems were planted on purpose so Squint has something real to find: one-time codes that did not arrive on the evening of Oct 10, families abandoning Group platters at checkout about half the time, about one table request in seven failing with "reservation failed" for every group, promo abuser accounts sharing devices, a payment tracker that went silent on one app version, lost rows on one day, an unmapped event property and a double-fired checkout event. Office groups putting down large deposits and students ordering rice meals are also planted, as normal behavior that is not a problem. No real customer data is included.
